tasks.short: Plan the activity and gather materials, demonstrate the activity to the children, help them try it, and note who needs more help.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher plans the activity and gathers materials
Kindergarten teacher demonstrates activities to children
Kindergarten teacher helps children try the activity
Kindergarten teacher notes which children need more help

tasks.design: The kindergarten team keeps a shared activity library per theme in the school's document space ({DOCS}), with material lists and photos of earlier set-ups, so each teacher adapts rather than plans from scratch. Notes on who needs more help are quick tags in the pupil record ({OTHER}) on a tablet. Demonstrating and helping children stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each teacher planned activities alone and noted needs on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared document spaces and pupil records on tablets are common in schools.
tasks.still_hard: Young children need the activity shown in a way that fits this group today.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a child's mistake into the next step of the activity.

reach.learn: Whether the shared library is reused.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records and learning-goal tracking.

assumptions: Boundary: from the theme plan to the help list; remedial help is outside.
Input contract: themes set by the kindergarten team; fallback is planning alone.
Demonstrating and helping do not change.
Children's time does not change.
s4 is the teacher's first note of which children need more help and keeps its full time.
s1 keeps 80: the library saves planning from scratch, but gathering and setting out the materials is physical work and stays.
research_questions: Does the shared library cut planning time?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher adds photos of set-ups to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one class and few library entries fit, so s1 keeps 90 (2.0); high: several classes sharing themes (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose books for the theme, read to the whole class, read to small groups and talk about the story, and note which books were read.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher chooses books for the theme
Kindergarten teacher reads books to the entire class
Kindergarten teacher reads to small groups and talks about the story
Kindergarten teacher notes which books were read: on a list today; after the change the log is pre-filled with borrowed books and the teacher marks those read

tasks.design: The school library catalogue ({OTHER}) is searchable by theme and reading level, and borrowing a book for the class adds it to the reading log, so the teacher does not search shelves and only marks which borrowed books were read. Reading aloud and talking about stories stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Books were found on the shelves and the reading log kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: School library catalogues can be searched by theme and level.
tasks.still_hard: The best book for a group depends on what happened that morning.
tasks.human_edge: Doing the voices so the whole class leans in.

evidence.claim: School library catalogues can be searched by theme and reading level.

assumptions: Boundary: from the theme plan to the reading log; buying books is outside.
Input contract: catalogue kept by the school librarian; fallback is the shelves.
Reading aloud does not change.
Children's time does not change.
s4 keeps 60: a loan shows a book was borrowed, not read, so the teacher still marks each book read.
research_questions: Do teachers find theme books faster?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher tags new books by theme.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small book corner the teacher knows well and many books outside the catalogue, so s1 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 80 (2.7); high: a large school library used as designed (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with the child, talk with parents, discuss the child with the support coordinator, write notes in the pupil record, and prepare extra activities for children with special interests.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher guides and counsels children with adjustment problems or special academic interests
Kindergarten teacher talks with parents about the child
Kindergarten teacher discusses the child with the support coordinator
Kindergarten teacher writes conversation notes in the pupil record
Kindergarten teacher prepares extra activities for children with special interests

tasks.design: Conversation notes use a short template in the pupil record ({OTHER}) with agreed actions and a follow-up date, so nothing is forgotten; the teacher still writes the notes. Extra activities for children with special interests come from the team's shared activity library. Talking with the child, the parents and the support coordinator stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were written in free text and extra activities planned from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records offer note templates with follow-up dates.
tasks.still_hard: Adjustment problems at age four or five rarely have a quick answer.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a shy child join the group at play.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records with a module for development plans and learning-goal tracking.
Under the WMS, parents consent to rules on pupil data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the child's concern to the extra activities; formal support plans are outside.
Input contract: templates set by the support coordinator; fallback is free-text notes.
Talking with children, parents and the coordinator does not change.
Parents' time does not change.
Conversation notes are a first record: s4 keeps 85, saving only the layout and standard fields.
research_questions: Do agreed follow-ups happen on time?

incremental.description: Kindergarten teacher sets follow-up dates in the record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: notes rarely fit the template and the library has few activities for special interests, so s4 keeps 95 and s5 keeps 90 (1.2); high: both used as designed (4.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe children at play and work, write observation notes, fill in each child's development record, discuss concerns with the support coordinator, and ask parents to see the school nurse about health concerns.

steps.what: Kindergarten teacher observes children's performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Kindergarten teacher writes observation notes: on paper today, as tags and short notes on a tablet in the pupil record after the change
Kindergarten teacher gathers each child's observation notes for the development record
Kindergarten teacher evaluates each child's development and scores the development lines
Kindergarten teacher discusses concerns with the support coordinator
Kindergarten teacher asks parents to see the school nurse about health concerns

tasks.design: Observations are tagged on a tablet in the pupil record ({OTHER}) against the school's development lines, with a short note where needed, so they no longer go from paper into the record. At record time the teacher sees each child's tags and notes together and scores the development lines. No software scores or rates children. Observing, discussing concerns and talking with parents stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations were jotted on paper and copied into the record twice a year.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records on tablets take quick observation tags.
tasks.still_hard: Tagging on a tablet can distract from watching the children.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a quiet child has stopped playing with friends.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records with learning-goal tracking.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3, so no software scores the children here.

assumptions: Boundary: from class activities to the health referral; formal support plans are outside.
Input contract: development lines set by the school; fallback is paper notes.
Observing and discussing do not change.
Parents' time does not change.
Writing observation notes is a first record and keeps its full time; only gathering the notes per child (s3 at 25) saves time, because they no longer go from paper into the record.
research_questions: Are development records complete on time?

incremental.description: No new ongoing work; learning the tagging set is one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many notes stay on paper during busy activities, so gathering keeps 60 (2.4); high: most observations tagged on the tablet (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The kindergarten teacher keeps demonstrating, reading, counselling and observing; planning alone, paper notes and copying into records shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time on the floor with the children.
